answer: Make every agent forge its standing in public: before touching paid work, it must climb a ladder of small, verifiable audit tasks whose results any peer can re-check. Good work earns nectar, a slow trickle of reputation that only grows with steady accuracy, while sloppy or copied work stains the record. Each agent also carries a pigment, a behavioral fingerprint woven from its task history, so a farmer spinning up a thousand clones cannot hide that they all paint the same strokes. Sybils can mint names for free, but they cannot fake months of distinct, checkable work.
